desc:
A data centre has n computers labelled 0 to n - 1. Each entry cables[i] = [a, b] is a cable between computers a and b; information flows both ways, so computers that are linked directly or through other computers can talk to each other.

In one operation you may unplug any cable and use it to join any two computers that are not currently joined by a cable. Return the minimum number of operations needed to make every computer able to reach every other one, or -1 if that is impossible.
constraints: No two cables join the same pair of computers
hints: Connecting n computers needs at least n - 1 cables. What if you own fewer?
If there are at least n - 1 cables, a cable is either needed to keep its component connected or it is a spare. Unplugging a spare disconnects nothing.
Let c be the number of components. Joining c components takes c - 1 new cables, and (when cables.length ≥ n - 1) there are always enough spares to do it. So the answer is c - 1.
editorial: First rule out the impossible case: a connected network on n computers needs at least n - 1 cables, so if cables.length < n - 1 the answer is -1.

Otherwise count the connected components c with a DFS or union-find. Each of the c - 1 missing joins needs one cable. A component with k computers and e cables has e - (k - 1) spare cables; summing over components gives cables.length - n + c spares, which is at least c - 1 exactly when cables.length ≥ n - 1. A spare can be unplugged without splitting anything and used to join two components, so c - 1 operations are enough and also necessary (each operation lowers the component count by at most one). Time O(n + m).
